messages:
Alex: uploaded the follow-up RFC (link) for the cooperative preemption + batcher handshake. main goal: let scheduler inform the batcher about an incoming latency fence so the batcher can finish/flush in a predictable way without dropping throughput. thoughts?
Marie: :wave: read it quickly. big +1 for explicit fence signals. question: do we want per-tenant fences or global fences only?
Alex: prefer per-tenant by default. global is just a broadcast convenience. per-tenant lets us avoid noisy neighbor stalls for small tenants.
Cheng: thinking about token accounting: if a fence arrives mid-batch, how do we attribute tokens to the flush vs next batch? we should avoid double-counting.
Pat: propose this contract: batcher exposes "startBatch(batchId, maxTokens) -> reservedTokens" and scheduler can call "injectFence(batchId, deadlineMs)". batcher then returns how many tokens were actually emitted before fence. we can derive billing from reservedTokens vs emittedTokens.
Samir: small nit: need a non-blocking acks path. scheduler can't synchronously wait on every batcher. use an async callback or event channel so fast-path requests aren't slowed.
Nina: agree with async callback. also add a metric for "fence-induced-flush-latency_ms" so we can measure tail impact.
Alex: here's a minimal pseudo API sketch: ```
// scheduler -> batcher
reserve(batchKey, maxTokens) -> reservationId
injectFence(reservationId, deadlineMs) -> fenceAck
// batcher behaviour
onFence(reservationId) { markBatchClosing(); emitUntil(deadlineMs or tokensConsumed==reserved); }
```
Cheng: race concern: what if a new high-priority request arrives after reserve but before injectFence? priority inversion. scheduler needs to be able to bump admission credits and potentially preempt. do we allow preempt-to-front or only preempt by stopping accumulation?
Marie: I'd prefer 'stop-accumulate + drain' as default, preempt-to-front is more intrusive and will fragment batches causing perf loss. maybe an escape hatch for extreme latency SLOs.
Pat: agree. also want to avoid changing batcher's public contract too often. this handshake should be minimal and versioned. add a capability flag: "supportsFenceV1".
Samir: operationally, we should simulate this on canary infra with synthetic steady load + periodic fences to measure throughput regression. I can spin up tests.
Nina: add observability bits to the RFC: histograms for pre-fence queue length, post-fence emitted tokens, and time-to-drain. without those we won't know if policy helps.
Alex: action items: 1) Pat will draft a compact API spec and versioning notes. 2) Samir will add a perf test harness. 3) Nina will add the metrics + dashboard mock. 4) Marie/Cheng to write up priority/preemption policy appendix. I'll open a PR for code-level hooks after those land.
ops-bot: uploaded RFC revision 2 at /rfc/cooperative-preemption-v2.md :eyes:
Marie: sounds good. can we also document billing edge-case where reserved > emitted so finance doesn't get surprised? small paragraph in API docs should suffice.
Alex: yes — will add billing paragraph. thanks all, this is actionable. :thumbsup:
Pat: I'll start the API draft today and tag y'all.
Samir: starting perf job tomorrow morning. will post numbers here.
Nina: I'll sketch dashboard wireframe by EOD.
Alex: let's reconvene next Tue to decide merge window. closing for now.
